passage: Saturday. Today Akash's face was red when I found him near the gate. Three boys from the next lane were laughing at his stammer and calling him names. My hands went cold. I wanted to shout, but I walked over, stood beside him and said, "That is my cousin. Please stop." My voice shook, but it came out calm. One boy smirked and they walked off, still muttering. Akash held my sleeve all the way home and whispered, "Thank you, didi." I told Chachi what happened, just in case they come back. I did not need to hit anyone, and I am glad. Aparna.

qa.a: She found Akash near the gate.

qa.q: What was Aparna feeling as she walked over to the boys?
qa.a: She was scared and angry: her hands went cold and she wanted to shout, but she stayed calm.

qa.q: Why did telling Chachi help, even though the boys had left?
qa.a: Telling an adult means someone else knows and can step in if the teasing returns, so Aparna and Akash are not alone with it.

qa.q: How might Akash have felt when Aparna stood beside him?
qa.a: Akash probably felt protected and relieved, which is shown by how he held her sleeve all the way home. 🤍

grounding: A child steps in calmly beside her small cousin who is being teased, then tells an adult; fighting was not needed.
